prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions, and setting; use specific action verbs and name clear maneuvers, indicate movement direction(s) relative to the camera/frame using a consistent order—horizontal first (toward/away/left-to-right/right-to-left/past) then vertical (upward/downward)—and state whether motions are simultaneous or sequential; describe body posture with concrete terms (standing, slightly leaning forward/back, seated, reclining, crouching, mid-jump, arms outstretched, knees bent) rather than interpretive labels, and report facial expressions or visible affect only when clearly evident using observable detail (open‑mouthed, smiling with teeth visible, furrowed brow) while specifying gaze targets (e.g., "eyes looking up at the kite," "gaze fixed on the camera"); specify precise spatial relationships, scale, and proximity (next to, behind, in front of, atop, touching, a few feet/meters apart, clustered closely, spread apart, in a line) and clarify subjects’ positions relative to each other and to background elements (e.g., "a third person seated at the far end," "man across from him"); for gestures state the direction and intended target (e.g., "gesturing with his right hand toward the person across from him"); note the number and arrangement of people (isolated individual, a small group clustered on benches, a line of pedestrians) and describe interaction dynamics only when supported by clear visual cues (hugging, holding hands, reaching, petting); describe lighting and shadows with observable cues—light quality (diffuse/overcast, directional backlight, strong side light), where shadows fall (onto ground, faces, building), and approximate shadow direction or length (casting long shadows toward the lower left, faint soft shadows); include visible surface textures or effects such as wet pavement, puddles, splashes, reflections, motion blur, or dust when present; keep the caption concrete, image‑centered, and avoid speculation or subjective judgments, and output exactly one single sentence (no lists, tags, multiple candidates, or metadata).
